cards.explanation: The answer is a cup of wine. The LORD, the God of Israel, says, “Take from My hand this cup of the wine of wrath…” (Jeremiah 25:15). It comes straight from His hand into Jeremiah's. This is not a cup you pass around at a party, and I'd say the prophet knew it.

The answer is nations. The LORD tells Jeremiah to “…make all the nations to whom I send you drink from it.” (Jeremiah 25:15). Later the passage lists them, from Jerusalem and the cities of Judah to the kings of the north (Jeremiah 25:18-26). I think this is one of the heavy parts of the book.

The answer is False. The word isn't famine, friends, it's the sword. The LORD says they “…will drink and stagger and go out of their minds, because of the sword that I will send among them.” (Jeremiah 25:16). Paying attention to one little word like that is how bakers get sharp.

The answer is True. Jeremiah says, “So I took the cup from the LORD’s hand…” (Jeremiah 25:17). Then he makes all the nations drink from it, each one to whom the LORD had sent him. I think that was a heavy thing to carry.

The answer is that they must drink it anyway. If they refuse, Jeremiah is to say that the LORD of Hosts says, “You most certainly must drink it!” (Jeremiah 25:28). There's no opting out of this one, friends. Saying no doesn't make the cup go away.

The answer is the city that bears His Name. The LORD says, “…I am beginning to bring disaster on the city that bears My Name…” (Jeremiah 25:29). This message already named Jerusalem at the head of the list (Jeremiah 25:18). Then He asks, “…how could you possibly go unpunished?”

The answer is all the inhabitants of the earth. The LORD of Hosts says, “…I am calling down a sword upon all the inhabitants of the earth…” (Jeremiah 25:29). He starts with the city that bears His Name, and the sword is for everyone on earth. Nobody gets skipped.

The answer is that He will roar. Jeremiah is to say, “The LORD will roar from on high…” (Jeremiah 25:30). Then it says He will “…roar loudly over His pasture…” That's a LOUD one, friends, and my mustache is standing straight up just reading it.

The answer is that the LORD brings a charge against the nations. The verse says, “The tumult will resound to the ends of the earth because the LORD brings a charge against the nations.” (Jeremiah 25:31). That's a courtroom word, and the text says He brings judgment on all mankind. The sound goes out to the ends of the earth.
The answer is False. This is a heavy verse, friends. It says those slain by the LORD on that day “…will not be mourned, gathered, or buried.” (Jeremiah 25:33). I think it's one to read slowly.

The answer is to wail and cry out. The text says, “Wail, you shepherds, and cry out; roll in the dust, you leaders of the flock.” (Jeremiah 25:34). The shepherds here are the leaders of the flock. The days of their slaughter have come.

The answer is True. The text says, “Flight will evade the shepherds, and escape will elude the leaders of the flock.” (Jeremiah 25:35). The verse before says, “…the days of your slaughter have come…” (Jeremiah 25:34). I think this is one of the heavy parts.

The answer is pasture. The text says, “…the LORD is destroying their pasture.” (Jeremiah 25:36). The shepherds lead the flock, so the pasture is their place. Then the next verse says the peaceful meadows have been silenced (Jeremiah 25:37).

The answer is the sword of the oppressor. The text says, “…their land has been made a desolation by the sword of the oppressor, and because of the fierce anger of the LORD.” (Jeremiah 25:38). Both are in the same line. A sword was in the message from the very beginning, back at the cup (Jeremiah 25:16).
